note: Planning only. Paths are PROPOSED. Every test is PLANNED - not implemented, not executed.
sources: prd-rebuild.md (shared PRD, kept outside this repo)

tasks.title: Monorepo, tooling and isolated test harness
tasks.objective: Set up the pnpm monorepo foundation and a test suite that runs locally from a clean checkout: each test worker has its own Postgres 16 database and MinIO bucket, with a guard that rejects production URLs.

scenarios: Tests stop immediately if DATABASE_URL points to a host other than localhost or the database name does not end in _test
Reject S3 endpoints other than local MinIO
2 parallel test workers create 2 different databases; writes with the same id do not conflict
Cleanup deletes only databases created by the test itself

done: `pnpm test` passes on a new machine with only Docker + Node
The production guard has a failing test before it passes
docs/testing.md includes commands to run from a clean checkout

tasks.title: Database foundation: Drizzle schema, migrations and conventions
tasks.objective: Set up packages/db with the PRD conventions (text nanoid PKs, no Postgres enums, timestamptz), ordered migrations, and foundation tables for users, sessions, stores, audit_log.

scenarios: All migrations run successfully on an empty database; a second run changes nothing
No Postgres enum types exist in the schema after migration (query pg_type)
newId() generates strings matching the contract's pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,40}$

done: Migrations run on an empty database and are idempotent
The schema follows the conventions, with tests to verify them

tasks.title: Email and password sign-in, admin-created accounts, invites
tasks.objective: Use better-auth with email and password, sessions stored in Postgres, and public signup disabled. Admins create accounts with temporary passwords (a change is required on first sign-in) or create invite links; invitees enter their own names and passwords. SMTP is not required.

scenarios: Tokens are stored only as hashes, with no plaintext in the database
Reusing an accepted token is rejected (replay)
A token expired after 7 days is rejected
A revoked token is rejected
Inviters cannot grant permissions they do not have (privilege escalation through invites)
Only someone with store.members for the target store can create an invite to that store
Calling the better-auth sign-up endpoint directly returns an error and creates no user
Accounts with temporary passwords are blocked from every page except the password change page
An admin creates an invite and copies the link; a new user opens the link, sets a password, and can enter the app
Signing out revokes the session in the database

done: All bypass, replay, expiry, revocation, and privilege escalation scenarios have failing tests before they pass
No user creation path exists outside admin creation and invites

tasks.title: Store-scoped permissions, ownership transfer and audit log
tasks.objective: Use a store_members table with preset roles and permissions[]; can(principal, permission, {storeId}) in packages/core is the sole permission check; audit_log records actor_user_id and actor_kind for every permission change and sensitive action. Stores & members screen (screen 5).

scenarios: The preset x permission matrix matches ADR 0002 (table-driven tests)
System admins do not have product.push or product.publish in stores where they have not been granted those permissions
seller_support does not have product.publish by default
Permissions for store A cannot be used in store B
Only the owner can grant product.publish
No one can grant permissions they do not have
The last owner cannot be deleted or demoted
Each store has exactly 1 owner (database constraint, 2 racing transactions)
Only the owner or an admin can transfer ownership, with an audit_log entry
The owner enables publish for co_leader, and co_leader sees the Public button; disabling it makes the button disappear
Permission states are shown with text and icons, not color alone

done: Every store-related server action goes through can()
The permission matrix has table-driven tests
Every permission change has an audit_log entry

tasks.title: Object storage, assets and per-store design library
tasks.objective: Upload directly to S3 using presigned PUT, verify sha256, deduplicate by (store_id, sha256), and read images through short-lived presigned GET URLs. Designs are store-scoped by default until a shared-use policy is finalized.

scenarios: Uploading a file with an incorrect declared sha256 causes finalization to be rejected and the object to be deleted
Uploading the same file 2 times in 1 store creates 1 asset
Members of store B cannot obtain presigned URLs for images in store A
Presigned URLs expire at the configured time
By default, a design appears only in the store where it was uploaded
Sharing a design with another store requires permission and an audit_log entry

done: No file read path bypasses store permission checks
Deduplication and checksum verification have tests

tasks.title: AI job lease table, fair scheduler and reaper
tasks.objective: Use a generation_jobs table with lease_token, lease_expires_at, attempt, error_class, priority; claim with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED ordered by tier, store rotation, requester rotation, and job age; the reaper returns jobs with expired leases to the queue; use provider_accounts and workers tables.

scenarios: 50 parallel claims on 20 jobs: no job is claimed 2 times
Store A has 200 jobs and store B has 2 jobs: B's jobs are claimed within the first 2 turns
An account missing a required provider skill does not receive jobs requiring that skill
An account in cooldown or with an expired session cannot claim jobs
Error class table: each class produces the correct job state, account state, and decision on whether to count an attempt
Transitions use UPDATE guarded by status + lease_token; only 1 of 2 racing updates wins
Cancellation wins over completion: if cancel is recorded first, complete returns job_not_active
A job whose lease expires without complete/fail returns to queued and counts as 1 transient attempt
Exceeding maxAttempts results in failed; being returned more than N times due to account errors results in failed with the reason that no healthy account is available

done: Tests verify no double claims under parallel load
Store-level fairness has tests
Every transition is a guarded UPDATE

tasks.title: Worker API v2 routes and worker tokens
tasks.objective: Implement packages/contracts exactly (OpenAPI 3.1, X-Contract-Version: 2) under /api/worker/v2: register, long-poll claim, heartbeat, uploads, complete, fail, account status, skill version. Each worker has its own token, stored as a hash. The worker team (ngatruong123) approves the contract before work begins.

scenarios: Every response matches the OpenAPI schema (validated with Ajv from packages/contracts)
An old lease returns 409 lease_lost
Repeating complete with the same Idempotency-Key returns the first result and creates no duplicate results
The same key with a different body returns 422 idempotency_key_reused
A missing uploadKey or mismatched sha256 returns 422
A missing or incorrect X-Contract-Version returns 426
A revoked token returns 401
Cancel and complete are sent simultaneously 100 times: the job always ends in exactly 1 state, and uploaded files from the losing branch are cleaned up

done: Contract tests pass for all examples in packages/contracts/examples
The worker team (ngatruong123) confirms the contract in writing (comment/issue)

tasks.title: tools/fake-worker per the contract
tasks.objective: A Node fake worker communicates only through Worker API v2 and presigned URLs, with scenarios for success, slow execution with heartbeat, rate limiting, session expiry, a mid-run crash, and returning an image with an incorrect checksum. Used for development, E2E, and load testing.

scenarios: success scenario: the job reaches succeeded with all images present
rate_limited scenario: the account enters cooldown, the job returns to queued, and attempt does not increase
crash scenario: the reaper returns the job to the queue after the lease expires
The worker rejects URLs outside storageOrigins

done: Runs with 1 command, with scenarios configured through arguments
Does not import internal apps/web code (uses only contracts)

tasks.title: Studio screen: design library, upload, job creation, queue
tasks.objective: Screen 1 follows the prototype: a virtualized design grid, URL-based filtering and search (nuqs), bulk uploads including entire folders, a mockup/redesign creation drawer for selecting a skill and quantity, and a queue drawer with position, status, cancel, and rerun.

scenarios: Upload 20 files with 1 duplicate: 19 new designs, with the duplicate clearly reported
Create a mockup job for 10 images: the job appears in the queue with its position
Cancel a running job: its displayed status changes to Cancelled
Filtering and search persist after reload (URL state)
axe reports no serious violations
The drawer traps focus; Esc closes it and returns focus to the opening button

done: The upload -> create job -> view in queue flow works with fake-worker
A grid of 1,000 designs scrolls smoothly (virtual list)

tasks.title: Image review screen
tasks.objective: Screen 2: the original design is shown beside the results; keyboard shortcuts A to approve, R to reject (a reason is required), arrows to switch images, and bulk approval; rejection reasons are stored to measure skill quality.

scenarios: Users without permission in the design's store cannot approve it
Rejection without a reason is refused
A approves, R opens the reason dialog, and arrows switch images
Keyboard shortcuts do not activate while typing in an input
Review states are shown with text + icons, not color alone
No horizontal overflow at 390px

done: 50 images can be reviewed using only the keyboard
Rejection reasons are stored with the job's skill_version_id

tasks.title: Realtime status (SSE) and usage_events recording
tasks.objective: Store-scoped SSE is sourced from Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY after commit; each finished job records usage_events (job_id, job_type, provider, account_id, requester_id, store_id, store_owner_id_at_time, units). There are no limits or quotas.

scenarios: A succeeded job records exactly 1 usage_event; repeating complete records no additional event
If the owner changes later, previous usage retains the original store_owner_id_at_time
A client for store A does not receive events for store B
Events are emitted only after commit; rollback emits no event

done: The queue updates without polling
Usage aggregation queries by store and by owner are available (read-only)

tasks.title: Product analysis
tasks.objective: A product_analysis job follows the contract: inputs are a design + niche + optional competitor link; outputs are audience, occasion, primary/secondary keywords, selling angle, product type and price suggestions, and IP warnings. Results provide context for content.

scenarios: A payload that does not match ProductAnalysisPayload causes the job to fail with input_invalid; no invalid data is stored
An IP warning at the high level is prominently displayed but does not block actions
Run analysis with fake-worker; the results display all sections

done: Analysis can be attached to a content job as context

tasks.title: Generate and edit multilingual listing content
tasks.objective: A listing_content job runs for each locale; the locale comes from params, not from the payload; pass the list of primary keywords already used in the store; the editor includes SEO limit counters, per-field regeneration, and version history; manual edits take precedence over newly generated content.

scenarios: The payload specifies a locale different from params: store according to params
A primary keyword duplicates a keyword already used in the store: show a warning
Manual edits are not overwritten by a later generation job
SEO rules from PRD §6.3 are covered by table-driven tests
Edit the title; the counter updates; save and reload, and the edit persists

done: Each locale has valid content before pushing is allowed

tasks.title: Catalog: product types, price tables, variants
tasks.objective: product_types and pricing_rules are store-scoped; variants are generated from the price table, not from a Cartesian product; ordered by sort_order; excluded_markets are specified per price row. Only users with store.settings can edit them.

scenarios: The number of variants exactly matches the number of price table rows, in sort_order order (invariant §20.1)
A price row missing an option for its type is rejected
Users without store.settings cannot edit the price table

done: The price table is editable in a table view, with validation

tasks.title: Create products from approved results
tasks.objective: Select a design + approved images and a product type; the SKU is the design filename without its extension; the design image is featured; product stage is derived according to PRD §5.3, calculated in batches rather than N+1.

scenarios: The SKU equals the filename without its extension and is the same for all variants (invariant §20.11)
Only approved images can be selected
Repeated creation from the same source does not create duplicate products
deriveStage branches from PRD §5.3 are covered by table-driven tests
Stages for a list of 200 products are calculated with a fixed number of queries

done: Created products have all variants, images, and SKUs

tasks.title: Shopify connection: encrypted credentials and client
tasks.objective: Store client_secret and access tokens using AES-256-GCM (a versioned key from env); the Shopify Admin GraphQL client handles throttling; include a Test connection button and a deterministic Shopify stub for tests.

scenarios: Encryption followed by decryption returns the original value; changing 1 byte of ciphertext causes decryption to fail
Logs and errors never contain secrets (string scan)
Shopify throttling triggers a wait and bounded retries
Only the owner or users with store.settings can view/edit credentials

done: No plaintext secrets in the database, logs, or responses

tasks.title: Push dry-run and snapshots
tasks.objective: A dry-run builds all push inputs (productSet, media, translations, markets, sales channels) from a content snapshot taken when the button is clicked, compares them with existing Shopify data, and displays the diff. Price or content changes after the dry-run invalidate it.

scenarios: The snapshot locks content at push time (invariant §20.10)
Changing prices after a dry-run marks it as stale and prevents pushing
A dry-run calls no mutations on the Shopify stub

done: Pushing is not allowed without a valid dry-run

tasks.title: Push draft: execution, permission recheck, idempotency, reconcile
tasks.objective: Push jobs run in apps/jobs (pg-boss); the first push defaults to draft; recheck product.push at execution time and before each store; a timeout after a Shopify write triggers a read to reconcile, not blind retries; every step records an event.

scenarios: Permission is revoked during a job: stop before the next store and record an event
An admin without a grant is rejected
Match variants using variantOptionKey, not by index (invariant §20.2)
Media: attach new images before deleting old ones (invariant §20.6)
The first push defaults to draft (invariant §20.9)
The stub times out after creating a product: the job reads it back by handle/idempotency key and does not create a second product
pg-boss redelivers a message: if the job is already terminal, exit immediately

done: Push 1 product to a Shopify dev store (a separate gate requiring credentials) with the correct variants, prices, and images

tasks.title: Publishing: active status, sales channels, markets
tasks.objective: Keep product.publish as a separate permission; the confirmation dialog requires a checked checkbox; recheck permission at execution time; market exclusion fails closed; other non-market sales channels are unpublished when declared by the type. Test the push-related PRD §20 invariants.

scenarios: Users with product.push but without product.publish are rejected
seller_support without publish permission granted by the owner is rejected
The owner revokes publish after a job is queued: the job stops at execution time
Market exclusion fails closed (invariant §20.3)
Other non-market channels are unpublished (invariant §20.4)

done: Every push-related §20 invariant has a corresponding test

tasks.title: Push request queue
tasks.objective: Users with product.edit but without product.push see the Send push request button; requests include a dry-run; users with product.push in the store approve or return requests with a reason; notifications are provided.

scenarios: Requesters cannot approve their own requests without product.push
A stale request dry-run must be rerun before approval
A seller submits a request, the owner sees it in the queue, and approval starts the push job

done: No push path bypasses a user with permission

tasks.title: Import and resync from Shopify
tasks.objective: Import existing Shopify products into the catalog; resync variants according to the price table; preserve SKUs during resync.

scenarios: Importing 2 times creates no duplicates
Resync preserves SKUs (invariant §20.11)
Users without store permission cannot import

done: Import runs in the background with progress and logs

tasks.title: Skill lifecycle: draft, review, publish, deprecate
tasks.objective: Skills and skill_versions are immutable according to the manifest in packages/contracts; check that template variables match their declarations; diff 2 versions; users with skill.publish approve; jobs record skill_version_id; assign default skills by job type, product type, and niche.

scenarios: Editing a published version is rejected; a new version must be created
A template using undeclared variables is rejected on save
A manifest that does not match the schema is rejected with the error path
Prompts render the correct variables; unexpected variables cannot be injected from user input

done: Every AI job can be traced to the correct skill version

tasks.title: Niche agent packages: safe zip upload and validator
tasks.objective: Upload niche skill zip files; extraction checks paths and limits size and file count; run the pod-skill-builder Python validator as a subprocess with a timeout, and map errors to fields.

scenarios: A zip containing ../ or absolute paths is rejected (zip-slip)
A zip bomb exceeding the extraction limit is stopped
Exceeding the maximum file count is rejected
Symlinks in zip files are rejected
A validator exceeding its time limit is killed and returns a clear error
Validator output maps correctly to fields

done: No files are written outside the temporary directory for that extraction

tasks.title: Provider skills: install tracking and routing
tasks.objective: Track which provider skill versions each account has installed (from register and account status); the scheduler assigns jobs requiring a skill only to accounts with that skill installed; run A/B trials and measure image approval rates by skill version.

scenarios: An account reports uninstalling a skill: jobs requiring it are no longer assigned to that account
Approval rates are calculated correctly by skill version x provider

done: It is possible to see which skills achieve better approval rates

tasks.title: AI account and worker screen (admin)
tasks.objective: The operations section of screen 6: account states (running, resting, session expired, waiting for worker), online workers and last heartbeat, running jobs, installed skills; a Re-login completed button; issue and revoke worker tokens (shown 1 time, stored as hashes).

scenarios: A worker token is shown only 1 time; the database contains only its hash
Revoke a token: the next request returns 401
Only admins can access it
Accounts with expired sessions are clearly shown with text + icons; clicking Re-login completed waits for worker confirmation

done: Admins can immediately identify accounts needing re-login

tasks.title: Security hardening
tasks.objective: Rate limits for sign-in, invite creation, and the worker API; CSP and security headers; CSRF for server actions; storageOrigins to prevent SSRF; log redaction; dependency audit; a security review checklist before production.

scenarios: Incorrect passwords beyond the threshold cause temporary lockouts by account and IP
Tokens, cookies, and secrets in logs are redacted before writing
Every page has CSP, X-Frame-Options, and Referrer-Policy matching the configuration

done: The security checklist passes and has been reviewed

tasks.title: Usage observability and reporting
tasks.objective: Structured logs, metrics (queue depth, claim time, expired leases, account states), alerts when account sessions expire or the queue stalls; audit log viewing; usage reports by store and owner (read-only, no limits).

scenarios: Queue metrics match the actual count of queued jobs in the database
An account transitions to session_expired: exactly 1 alert, no spam

done: An operations dashboard is sufficient for on-call work without reading the database

tasks.title: Load testing per profile and pass gates
tasks.objective: Measure on real Postgres and MinIO using fake-worker. Proposed profiles: A = 50 UI users + 20 accounts + 5,000 jobs; B = 200 users + 100 accounts + 50,000 jobs. Proposed pass gates (finalize once the production machine is available): claim p95 < 200 ms, no double claims, no store waits more than 3 rotations. Publish the machine configuration; capacity is measured, not a promise of unlimited scale.

scenarios: Profiles A and B run for the full duration and output p50/p95/p99, errors, fairness, and queue drain time

done: A report includes actual measurements and machine configuration
Document the thresholds requiring more workers or a separate database

tasks.title: UI polish and accessibility
tasks.objective: Review all 6 screens at 1440, 1024, 390: no horizontal overflow, complete keyboard operation, states not indicated by color alone, reduced motion, clean axe results, and screenshot comparisons to detect layout breakage.

scenarios: 6 screens x 3 sizes: no horizontal overflow; screenshots match the baseline within the threshold
axe reports no serious/critical violations on 6 screens
All main flows can be completed using only the keyboard

done: The UI checklist passes at all 3 sizes

tasks.title: Niche master data editor (schema 2.0)
tasks.objective: A 5-step form authors all 17 sections of schema 2.0; enforce per-field minimum counts as in the generator, with exactly 4 style_variants; errors use the validator's format, and the Fix button focuses the field; data states are curated-draft, researched, validated; drafts autosave under skill.edit permission.

scenarios: occasions with 6 records: error requires at least 8 records; found 6
style_variants with 5 records: error requires exactly 4
qa_rules.max_colors of 13: error expected an integer from 1 to 12
A palette containing #00FF00 is rejected
The sample data teacher-example-data.json is valid
The Fix button jumps to the correct step and focuses the field with the error
The build button is disabled while errors remain
No horizontal overflow at 1024, 760, 390px

done: The UI minimum rules and Python validator produce the same results on the sample dataset

tasks.title: Market-fit scoring and skill version builds from master data
tasks.objective: Score 6 criteria from 1 to 5 (clarity, gift suitability, emotion, differentiation, collection potential, IP safety), with a maximum of 30; 25 or more: proceed, 21: revise, 16: rework, 15 or less: replace; IP below 4 always blocks. Builds invoke the generator as a worker job with a timeout and produce an immutable skill_version that is not yet published.

scenarios: 26 points, IP 5: Proceed
24 points: Revise
IP 3 even with a total of 27: Block
15 points: Replace
The generator exceeds its time limit: the job reports a clear error and creates no version
A successful build creates a new version in draft state without automatically publishing

done: Every skill version built from master data can be traced to its master data version and scores

tasks.title: OpenBao secret store for subscription accounts and automatic re-login
tasks.objective: Store subscription account credentials (ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, Gemini, and other services) in OpenBao KV v2, with TOTP through the totp secrets engine. Workers authenticate using AppRole and receive secrets through single-use response wrapping. When account_state becomes session_expired, the worker automatically logs in again; captcha or device verification changes the state to waiting for a human and alerts admins. The webapp sees only metadata, never secret values.

scenarios: The webapp API returns account metadata without secret values
Using a wrap token a second time is rejected
The worker policy cannot read another store's path
session_expired: the worker reports successful re-login and the state returns to available
A captcha is encountered: the state changes to waiting for a human, and admins receive an alert

done: No passwords, cookies, or TOTP seeds are stored in Postgres, logs, or job payloads
